records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `--flusher-processes 0` is silently coerced to one process per shard via the `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback, giving operators maximum parallelism instead of a validation error when they intended to disable it.
records.rationale: The diff adds `max_processes: int | None = None` and sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` in `SpanFlusher.__init__`. Because `0` is falsy, passing `--flusher-processes 0` (the new click option has `type=int` and no validation/min bound) will be treated the same as `None` and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e., one process per shard (max parallelism) rather than 0 or an error. This is a real, verifiable behavior introduced by the diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backpressure metric `spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure` is incremented inside the per-process loop, so one submit can fire the counter N times before a single `MessageRejected`, inflating the backpressure rate metric up to flusher-process-count-fold.
records.rationale:
In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the metric increment is immediately followed by `raise MessageRejected()` inside the per-process loop, so a single `submit` call cannot increment `spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure` N times. The diff shows:

```py
for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values():
    if (...):
        metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")
        raise MessageRejected()
```

Because the exception exits the function on the first triggering process, at most one increment can occur per `submit`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead guard `if not process: continue` in flusher.py — processes dict values are never falsy and `is_alive()` already handles dead processes; the guard implies an absent-process state that cannot occur
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the loop has `if not process: continue` before calling `process.is_alive()`. From the diff, `self.processes` is only populated with `process = make_process(...)` objects in `_create_process_for_shards` (`self.processes[process_index] = process`), and there is no assignment of `None`/falsy values anywhere. Both `multiprocessing.Process` and `threading.Thread` instances are truthy, so this guard is effectively unreachable/redundant and implies a state (“absent process”) that the shown code never creates.
